Published online:
    September 4, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (primary: Japan, USA; secondary: New Zealand, Australia)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    The yen posted its strongest weekly gain since late July despite a Friday pullback, driven by rising BOJ rate hike expectations ahead of the Sept 17-18 meeting. The dollar index slipped ~0.7% on the week. Markets are focused on incoming NFP data and next week's CPI print ahead of the Sept 15-16 Fed meeting. Fed Governor Waller signaled a hold preference if inflation continues moderating, cutting September hike odds back to ~50%. Elevated crude oil above $95 (post-US strikes on Iran) keeps inflation risk alive. JPMorgan warns of potential dollar weakness to 142-146/yen if yen shorts unwind.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (the Fed rate decision, NFP, and CPI data are central drivers of the narrative alongside yen dynamics)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 50 (market is split; a September hike remains live at 50% implied probability)
Probability of increase: 50%

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 60 (Waller's dovish lean and pared bets tilt the narrative slightly toward a hold)
Probability of holding: 50%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 5 (no meaningful discussion of cuts; crude above $95 and sticky inflation make cuts implausible near-term)
Probability of decrease: ~0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: -25 (Mildly dovish — Waller's Thursday comments leaning toward a hold if inflation moderates pulled September hike bets back to 50%, but geopolitical inflation risk from elevated crude keeps the door open to a hike, preventing a fully dovish read)
